COND-C02-COVIDOUT-2022: The COVID-OUT randomized placebo-controlled trial evaluated metformin, ivermectin and fluvoxamine for acute COVID-19.
People with acute COVID-19; the existing ivermectin outcome record identifies the 808 participants in its relevant comparison. This is not a count of participants across every trial arm.
The ivermectin comparison did not demonstrate a reduction in the composite of hypoxemia, emergency care, hospitalization or death.

The result concerns a specific acute-treatment composite. It does not establish efficacy for cancer or for treating established Long COVID, and related COVID-OUT reports are not additional independent trials.
P-D08-ACTIV6-2023: ACTIV-6 compared a six-day higher-dose ivermectin schedule with placebo for time to sustained recovery.
Outpatients with mild to moderate COVID-19.
The tested schedule did not shorten sustained recovery.
This randomized clinical result does not support a recovery benefit from the tested regimen. It addresses patients and recovery directly, unlike cell-culture antiviral experiments.
P-D08-ANTIVIRAL-2023: Laboratory experiments examined whether membrane effects could explain ivermectin’s in vitro antiviral activity.
Cell-culture and membrane models, rather than patients receiving a COVID-19 treatment.
Antiviral effects occurred at concentrations above reported toxic clinical concentrations and were associated with nonspecific membrane effects.
The exposure and membrane findings limit translation from antiviral activity in vitro to a usable human treatment. They do not establish that higher dosing would provide clinical benefit.
P-D08-OVARIAN-2009: Cell-culture experiments examined PAK1 activity and growth after ivermectin exposure.
Human ovarian cancer and NF2-deficient schwannoma cell models.
The reported findings link PAK1 inhibition with suppressed cell growth.
The experiment supports a mechanistic hypothesis in these cell models. It did not measure patient survival or symptoms and cannot supply a clinical cancer-benefit estimate.
P-D08-GBM-2016: Preclinical experiments examined mitochondrial respiration, oxidative stress and tumor growth under ivermectin exposure.
Glioblastoma cells and experimental tumor models.
Mitochondrial respiration inhibition and increased oxidative stress accompanied growth suppression.
The findings identify an experimental growth-inhibition mechanism. Their presence in tumor models does not demonstrate a safe or effective glioblastoma treatment in people.
P-D08-BREAST-2016: Experiments examined PAK1 degradation, Akt/mTOR signaling and autophagy after ivermectin exposure.
Breast cancer cell and animal models.
PAK1 degradation and reduced Akt/mTOR signaling were associated with growth-arresting autophagy.
The study links a pathway change to an experimental growth effect. It does not establish improved clinical outcomes or a human breast-cancer dosing schedule.
P-D08-CRC-2014: Cell and animal experiments tested WNT-TCF pathway responses and tumor growth, including pathway-rescue and comparison models.
WNT-dependent human cancer models, including colorectal cancer cells and mouse xenografts.
Forcing TCF signaling back on rescued cells from some low-concentration effects. Ivermectin inhibited TCF-dependent xenografts but not the TCF-independent comparison model.

The rescue and comparison experiments strengthen a specific mechanistic explanation. Tumor biology, exposure and formulation still limit clinical translation; this study is not an independent randomized patient trial.
P-D08-HCC-2022: The original report described preclinical experiments combining ivermectin with sorafenib. The report is retracted.
Hepatocellular carcinoma experimental models, rather than a clinical patient comparison.
No efficacy conclusion is retained from this retracted report.
The report remains traceable for source-integrity context only. Its reported effects cannot support a benefit grade, a combination mechanism or a treatment recommendation.
COND-C16-ALASCCA-2025: The randomized placebo-controlled adjuvant trial examined Cancer recurrence. The recorded comparison was Aspirin versus placebo.
Patients with PI3K-altered localized colorectal cancer.
Lower recurrence in prespecified hotspot group.
Molecularly selected population; severe adverse events 16.8% versus 11.6%; not all CRC
COND-C20-ASP-2020: The observational cohort in chronic viral hepatitis examined HCC incidence. The recorded comparison was Aspirin use versus nonuse in observational cohort.
Participants in an observational investigation of hepatocellular carcinoma and liver-related mortality; detailed eligibility is not on hand.
Lower incidence associated with aspirin use.
Observational association; prevention rather than established tumor treatment
P-D23-MYELOMA: Aspirin versus enoxaparin for thromboprophylaxis during lenalidomide-based myeloma treatment. Randomized open-label thromboprophylaxis substudy.
342 selected patients with newly diagnosed myeloma and low thromboembolic risk
Here the purpose is prevention of treatment-associated blood clots through antiplatelet action, rather than killing myeloma cells.

The finding concerns 342 selected patients with newly diagnosed myeloma and low thromboembolic risk. The reported design does not independently establish that the drug caused the observed clinical change.
CP015-ARTICLE: Immune cells transcriptome-based drug repositioning for multiple sclerosis. Original computational transcriptomic drug repositioning; no new drug trial.
Public relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis immune-cell transcriptome datasets, untreated versus healthy and pre/post fingolimod or interferon-beta; limited proteomic cross-check.
Original report; its design and outcome must be considered separately. Original computational transcriptomic drug repositioning; no new drug trial

Only fingolimod and interferon-beta treated datasets available; low DEG thresholds; restricted proteome validation; no basic or clinical trials of highlighted candidates (PDFp14). The complete pathway-drug supplementary lists are referenced but not printed in this supplied PDF (p15).
P-D23-OVARIAN: Aspirin blocks EGF-stimulated ovarian cancer-cell viability through COX-1. Laboratory mechanistic study.
COX-1-positive and negative ovarian cancer cell models
In COX-1-positive ovarian cancer cells, aspirin reduced EGF-driven Akt/Erk phosphorylation and cell viability. COX-1-negative cells responded differently.
The finding applies to COX-1-positive and negative ovarian cancer cell models. It does not establish patient benefit or a human treatment schedule.
P-D23-HNSCC: NSAID use and PIK3CA-altered head and neck cancer survival. Observational cohort with mechanistic experiments.

Research links the PI3K pathway with NSAID sensitivity. A patient cohort associated regular NSAID use with survival in PIK3CA-altered tumors, alongside preclinical testing including aspirin; the clinical observation was not aspirin randomization.
The finding applies to 266 patients and related preclinical models. It does not establish patient benefit or a human treatment schedule.
P-D13-PROSTATE-2018: Atorvastatin versus placebo for prostate cancer before radical prostatectomy: a randomized double-blind clinical trial. Randomized preoperative placebo-controlled trial.
No significant overall reduction in Ki-67 or PSA; subgroup findings exploratory.
The reported finding concerns 160 men randomized; 158 completed follow-up. Its applicability beyond that population and the reported outcome is not established by this source summary.
COND-C29-ATOR-2018: The randomized single-blind clinical trial examined VASI score change. The recorded comparison was Atorvastatin plus NB-UVB versus NB-UVB alone.
Patients with active vitiligo receiving narrowband UV-B.
30 randomized, 29 analyzed; small single-blind trial; adverse events in 10 combination participants
P-D13-GBM-2021: The prospective single-arm phase ii trial examined Progression-free survival proportion. The recorded comparison was Atorvastatin with chemoradiation; single arm.
The single-arm 36-patient study reported 66% progression-free at six months but concluded that improvement was not demonstrated.
Single-arm study; the reported progression-free proportion does not establish improvement over chemoradiation alone.
P-D13-BREAST-2013: The uncontrolled preoperative biomarker study examined Ki 67 relative change. The recorded comparison was Atorvastatin before surgery; baseline comparison.
50 patients enrolled with invasive breast cancer
Overall Ki-67 decreased by 7.6% (p=0.39); a larger decrease in the HMGCR-positive subgroup was exploratory and not a survival result.
Two-week uncontrolled presurgical study; Ki-67 is a proliferation biomarker, not recurrence or survival.
P-D13-AML-2019: Atorvastatin exerts antileukemia activity via inhibiting mevalonate-YAP axis in K562 and HL60 cells. Cell-culture experiments.
Cell-cycle and apoptosis effects implicated mevalonate-YAP signaling.
The finding applies to K562 and HL60 leukemia cells. It does not establish patient benefit or a human treatment schedule.
P-D15-BREAST-2021: The phase iii randomized placebo-controlled trial examined Disease-free survival. The recorded comparison was Celecoxib versus placebo after primary breast-cancer treatment.
REACT found no disease-free survival advantage: hazard ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.17).
Disease-free survival was not improved; the estimate applies to the REACT trial population.
P-D15-COLON-2021: The randomized placebo-controlled trial examined Disease-free survival. The recorded comparison was Celecoxib versus placebo alongside adjuvant chemotherapy.
Resected stage III colon cancer receiving adjuvant chemotherapy
Overall disease-free survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.03).
The confidence interval includes no difference and a potentially meaningful reduction in recurrence or death; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.
P-D15-HCC-2017: The randomized pilot combination trial examined Median overall survival. The recorded comparison was TACE plus celecoxib and lanreotide versus TACE.
Median survival was 15 months with TACE plus celecoxib and lanreotide versus 7.5 months with TACE alone; adding two drugs prevents assigning the benefit to celecoxib alone.
Pilot trial adding two drugs; the survival difference cannot be assigned to celecoxib alone.
P-D15-COLON-2024: Improved survival with adjuvant COX-2 inhibition in PIK3CA-activated stage III colon cancer: CALGB/SWOG 80702. Preplanned molecular subgroup analysis of randomized trial.
Patients from CALGB/SWOG 80702 with tumor sequencing
A PIK3CA gain-of-function subgroup showed benefit; not an independent trial.
The reported finding concerns Patients from CALGB/SWOG 80702 with tumor sequencing. Its applicability beyond that population and the reported outcome is not established by this source summary.
P-D15-LONGCOVID-2026: Patient-reported improvements from use of IMC-2 alone and IMC-2 and Paxlovid in a Long COVID cohort: a case series. Open-label convenience-sample case series.
24 completers receiving valacyclovir-celecoxib with or without Paxlovid
Patients reported symptom changes, but multidrug uncontrolled treatment cannot isolate celecoxib.
The finding concerns 24 completers receiving valacyclovir-celecoxib with or without Paxlovid. The reported design does not independently establish that the drug caused the observed clinical change.
P-D15-OVARIAN-2012: The DoCaCel randomized phase II study of celecoxib with docetaxel and carboplatin. Randomized phase II trial.
196 eligible patients with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
No significant PFS or OS advantage; early celecoxib discontinuation limited interpretation.

The reported finding concerns 196 eligible patients with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer. Its applicability beyond that population and the reported outcome is not established by this source summary.
P-D15-HEADNECK-2014: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of celecoxib for oral mucositis during head-and-neck radiotherapy. Randomized placebo-controlled trial.
Did not reduce mucositis severity, pain, dietary compromise or opioid use.
The reported finding concerns 40 head-and-neck cancer patients receiving radiotherapy. Its applicability beyond that population and the reported outcome is not established by this source summary.
P-D15-PANCREAS-2005: A phase II study of celecoxib, gemcitabine and cisplatin in advanced pancreatic cancer. Phase II combination study.
Addition of celecoxib did not appear to increase activity of the chemotherapy doublet.
The reported finding concerns Advanced pancreatic cancer. Its applicability beyond that population and the reported outcome is not established by this source summary.
CP002-R01: The original computational transcriptome/cmap drug repositioning examined Connectivity Map (CMap) enrichment score for a selected gene cluster. The recorded comparison was Transcriptomic cluster queried against Connectivity Map drug profiles; no treated-patient comparison.
GSE100833 anti-TNF refractory Crohn's disease inflamed and non-inflamed colonic transcriptomes; CMap and STRING analyses.

Vorinostat was nominated by an original computational analysis of Crohn disease transcriptomes. The result identifies a hypothesis for experimental testing and does not demonstrate symptom improvement, remission or clinical safety. Clomipramine was nominated by an original computational analysis of Crohn disease transcriptomes. The result identifies a hypothesis for experimental testing and does not demonstrate symptom improvement, remission or clinical safety.

Nonlinear biological systems cannot be fully modeled; selection bias from a single dataset may restrict generalizability; further studies in genetically diverse samples and in-depth experimental studies are required (PDF pp.6-7).
P-D18-GBM: The randomized controlled trial examined Survival and serious toxicity. The recorded comparison was Disulfiram and copper plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy.
No significant survival improvement; increased severe adverse events.
Small recurrent-disease trial; findings specific to combination
P-D17-PRINCIPLE: The randomized controlled trial examined Recovery; COVID-19 hospitalization or death. The recorded comparison was Doxycycline versus usual care.
Older or clinically vulnerable community patients with suspected COVID-19
No clinically meaningful recovery or hospitalization benefit.
Open-label community platform trial; suspected and confirmed infections
P-D17-BREAST: Preoperative doxycycline and cancer stem-cell markers in early breast cancer. Clinical pilot tissue study.
Nine doxycycline-treated patients and six untreated controls
Mitochondrial protein synthesis supports some stem-like tumor cells. A small preoperative pilot tested 14 days of doxycycline and measured CD44 and ALDH1, alongside other tissue markers.

The reported finding concerns Nine doxycycline-treated patients and six untreated controls. Its applicability beyond that population and the reported outcome is not established by this source summary.
P-D17-ORAL: Doxycycline effects on oral squamous carcinoma invasion and tumor growth. Laboratory and animal study.
SCC-15 oral squamous carcinoma cells and xenografts
In oral squamous carcinoma models, doxycycline reduced MMP-2/MMP-9 production and limited cell invasion and migration. The proposed target is tissue-degrading enzyme activity.
The finding applies to SCC-15 oral squamous carcinoma cells and xenografts. It does not establish patient benefit or a human treatment schedule.
P-D17-PANCREAS: Doxycycline induces apoptosis in PANC-1 pancreatic cancer cells. Laboratory and animal study.
PANC-1 pancreatic cancer cells and mouse xenografts
PANC-1 experiments found activation of proapoptotic genes, suppression of antiapoptotic Bcl-xL/Mcl-1, and reduced IL-8 expression, with growth suppression in mouse xenografts.
The finding applies to PANC-1 pancreatic cancer cells and mouse xenografts. It does not establish patient benefit or a human treatment schedule.
COND-C10-DOXY-2004: The multicenter randomized trial examined Clinical attachment level and probing depth. The recorded comparison was Scaling/root planing plus subantimicrobial doxycycline versus placebo.
Patients receiving scaling and root planing for periodontal disease.
Adjunctive regimen; not replacement for mechanical treatment
P-D10-LIVER-2024: Severe drug-induced liver injury due to self-administration of the veterinary anthelmintic medication, fenbendazole. Human case report.
Biopsy-confirmed severe liver injury; liver tests normalized after cessation.
The finding concerns 67-year-old woman self-administering fenbendazole. The reported design does not independently establish that the drug caused the observed clinical change.
P-D10-OVARIAN-2024: Transcriptome analysis reveals the anticancer effects of fenbendazole on ovarian cancer: an in vitro and in vivo study. Cell and mouse experiments.
A2780 and SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells and experimental tumors
Investigated apoptosis and mitotic catastrophe; preclinical ovarian-cancer evidence.
The finding applies to A2780 and SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells and experimental tumors. It does not establish patient benefit or a human treatment schedule.
P-D10-LIVER-2026: Differentiating fenbendazole-induced liver injury from immunotherapy hepatitis: a case report. Human case report.
47-year-old woman with metastatic colon cancer receiving nivolumab/relatlimab
Severe liver injury occurred after increased self-administered fenbendazole; highlights confounding with immunotherapy-associated hepatitis.

The finding concerns 47-year-old woman with metastatic colon cancer receiving nivolumab/relatlimab. The reported design does not independently establish that the drug caused the observed clinical change.
MECH-D10-MICROTUBULE-2018: The mechanistic laboratory study examined Excised xenograft size and weight. The recorded comparison was Fenbendazole versus untreated/control xenografts.
Human lung-cancer cell lines, purified bovine tubulin and A549 mouse xenografts

Fenbendazole reduced A549 xenograft size and weight in the reported mouse experiment, with supporting apoptosis and vascularity assays. This does not establish cancer control or safe dosing in people.
No human cancer trial or safe human anticancer exposure was established. Laboratory selectivity is not clinical safety.
P-D10-PROTEASOME-2012: Impairment of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway by methyl N-(6-phenylsulfanyl-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate leads to a potent cytotoxic effect in tumor cells: a novel antiproliferative agent with a potential therapeutic implication. Preclinical laboratory study.
human NSCLC and other cancer cell lines vs normal cells
Cancer-cell experiments found proteasome impairment and endoplasmic-reticulum stress. This report did not test antitumor efficacy in animals or people.
Nonclinical evidence does not establish benefit, safety or a cancer dose in people.
P-D10-VITAMINS-2008: Unexpected antitumorigenic effect of fenbendazole when combined with supplementary vitamins. Preclinical laboratory study.
SCID mice (C.B-17), 20 male 4-week-old mice in 4 diet groups, housed 5 per cage (as printed); human Burkitt lymphoma P493-6 xenograft
A small lymphoma mouse experiment found reduced tumor growth with fenbendazole plus supplemented vitamins. Fenbendazole alone did not differ significantly from control (P = 0.12).
Nonclinical evidence does not establish benefit, safety or a cancer dose in people.
P-D10-EMT6-DIET-2012: Use of fenbendazole-containing therapeutic diets for mice in experimental cancer therapy studies. Preclinical laboratory study.
BALB/c Rw mice, EMT6 tumors; 8 mice per group initially, 4 groups (as printed)
Fenbendazole-containing chow did not alter EMT6 mammary tumor growth, invasion, metastasis or response to local radiation in mice.
Nonclinical evidence does not establish benefit, safety or a cancer dose in people.
P-D10-EMT6-2013: Fenbendazole as a potential anticancer drug. Preclinical laboratory study.
EMT6 mouse mammary-tumor cells and tumors in mice
Intensive fenbendazole regimens did not improve EMT6 tumor growth or radiation response in mice, despite cell-culture toxicity.
Nonclinical evidence does not establish benefit, safety or a cancer dose in people.
P-D10-H4IIE-2022: Fenbendazole Suppresses Growth and Induces Apoptosis of Actively Growing H4IIE Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells via p21-Mediated Cell-Cycle Arrest. Preclinical laboratory study.
Fenbendazole inhibited actively growing H4IIE rat liver-cancer cells, but did not change glucose consumption or lactate production in this model.
Nonclinical evidence does not establish benefit, safety or a cancer dose in people.
P-D10-CRC-CELLS-2022: Anti-cancer effects of fenbendazole on 5-fluorouracil-resistant colorectal cancer cells. Preclinical laboratory study.
wild-type and 5-FU-resistant SNU-C5 human colorectal cells
The abstract reports cancer-cell effects in 5-fluorouracil-resistant colorectal cells without requiring p53. No patients were studied.
Nonclinical evidence does not establish benefit, safety or a cancer dose in people.
MECH-D34-HYPHAE-1999: Effects of Azole Antifungal Drugs on the Transition from Yeast Cells to Hyphae in Susceptible and Resistant Isolates of the Pathogenic Yeast Candida albicans. Mechanistic laboratory study.
Susceptible and resistant clinical Candida albicans isolates
Fluconazole inhibited hyphal development in susceptible Candida isolates under specified laboratory conditions. Resistant isolates could retain this invasive-growth trait.
Hyphal morphology is not direct measurement of human tissue invasion; results depended on strain, medium and exposure timing.
MECH-D34-BIOFILM-2019: Expression of fluconazole resistance-associated genes in biofilm from 23 clinical isolates of Candida albicans. Mechanistic laboratory study.
23 clinical Candida albicans isolates; eight selected for gene-expression measurements
Clinical Candida isolates became less susceptible to fluconazole as laboratory biofilms matured. The experiment does not support describing fluconazole as a general biofilm-destroying drug.
Plate biofilms and a nonstandardized biofilm inoculum limit clinical interpretation; prevention is distinct from eradication.
MECH-D07-HEDGEHOG-2010: Itraconazole, a commonly used anti-fungal that inhibits Hedgehog pathway activity and cancer growth. Mechanistic laboratory study.
Shh-Light2/NIH-3T3 reporter cells, pathway-mutant cells and mouse tumor allografts
Itraconazole suppressed Hedgehog signaling in reporter and tumor models, with experiments locating its action near Smoothened. Fluconazole did not share this activity in the tested assay.
Model-specific pathway inhibition is not a cancer-treatment outcome. Serum conditions materially changed potency.
